description: This topic covers the fundamental classification of programming languages used to communicate with computers. It explores the differences between high-level and low-level languages, as well as the essential system software like compilers and interpreters that translate them.

sections.title: Classification of Programming Languages
sections.description: Computer languages are primarily categorized into two main groups based on their proximity to the computer's hardware.

key_concepts.explanation: A formal set of syntax rules and symbols used to write computer programs and instruct the hardware to perform specific tasks.
A machine-friendly language that interacts closely with the computer's hardware. It is highly machine-dependent, memory-efficient, but difficult for humans to read or debug.
A user-friendly language that uses English-like vocabulary and mathematical symbols. It is machine-independent, portable across different systems, and easier to learn and maintain.

sections.title: Low-Level Languages
sections.description: The closest languages to the native hardware, understood directly by the computer's processor or with minimal translation.

key_concepts.explanation: The First Generation Language (1GL) consisting entirely of binary digits (0s and 1s). It is the only language directly understood by the CPU without requiring any translator.
The Second Generation Language (2GL) that uses short alphanumeric codes or mnemonics (e.g., ADD, SUB, MOV) instead of pure binary codes to write instructions.

important_facts.fact: Programs written in Machine Language execute the fastest among all languages because they do not require any intermediate translation steps.

sections.title: High-Level Languages and their Inventors
sections.description: Major high-level languages that revolutionized software development and their respective creators.

key_associations.extra_info: Developed in the 1950s, it was the first high-level programming language, widely used for complex scientific, engineering, and mathematical calculations.
Developed in 1972 at Bell Labs. It is a powerful procedural language often referred to as the 'mother of all programming languages'.
Developed by Sun Microsystems in 1995. It is strictly based on the 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' (WORA) principle, offering massive platform portability.
Highly popular for its extremely simple syntax, readability, and extensive libraries used in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Science.

sections.title: Language Translators
sections.description: Crucial system software designed to convert human-readable source code into machine-readable binary object code.

key_concepts.explanation: A type of system software that processes code written in a high-level or assembly language and converts it into native machine language.
A specialized translator that specifically converts Assembly language mnemonics into machine language (binary code).
A translator that scans and translates the entire high-level language program into machine code at once. It executes faster and lists all syntax errors simultaneously at the end of compilation.
A translator that reads, translates, and executes the high-level language program line-by-line. If it encounters an error, it stops execution immediately and reports it.

sections.title: Important Programming Facts
sections.description: Essential one-liner facts and terminologies related to programming concepts.

important_facts.fact: COBOL (Common Business Oriented Language) is an early high-level language primarily designed for business, finance, and administrative computing systems.
Source Code is the original, human-readable instructions written by the programmer, whereas Object Code is the machine-readable output generated by a compiler.
A Syntax Error occurs when a programmer violates the strict grammatical rules or structural rules of a programming language, which prevents the code from compiling.
A Bug is an error, flaw, or fault in a computer program that causes it to produce an incorrect or unexpected result, and the process of fixing it is known as Debugging.
